title: RAG Evaluation: Visual Guide
outline: 1. Three Separable Failures | three switches for the pipeline stages - retrieval delivered the evidence, the generator stuck to the context, the answer addressed the question - each flipping one metric family and printing the aggregated RAG score beside it | a RAG system fails in three separable places with three different owners, and a single averaged score moves for all of them and names none

2. Counting Atomic Claims | six atomic claims decomposed from one answer about the Team plan, tappable between supported and unsupported, with a strict-verifier toggle | faithfulness is supported claims over total claims (five of six = 0.83) and the unsupported claim names the defect - an absent number means retrieval or memory leakage, a contradiction means generation

3. Precision Versus Recall | eight retrieved chunks with a k slider, a rerank toggle and a switch that breaks the chunking carrying the annual-plan exception, computing plain precision, rank-aware precision and context recall | precision 3/8 = 0.375 and recall 1/2 = 0.5 are different failures - lost-in-the-middle means ordering changes the answer without changing the chunks, and low recall is a chunking audit before a retrieval one

4. Scorecard Not Score | three candidate answers to 'how do I cancel', each with seven dimensions grouped by owning team plus its online signal, and a toggle that collapses them to one averaged number | three answers whose aggregates sit within a few hundredths of each other need three unrelated repairs, so aggregation destroys the triage value that is the entire point of measuring

5. Calibrating The Judge | four judge-bias toggles (self-preference, verbosity, shallow agreement, drift) inflating the reported score above the human golden-set truth, with a slider for golden-set size and the +/-0.98/sqrt(n) interval | an LLM judge is a sensor, so its readings mean nothing until validated against a few hundred human labels, its version pinned, and the metric treated as a regression detector rather than truth
